title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Except Technical and Scientific Products

tasks.short: Answer buyer questions about products, prices, availability, uses and credit terms.

steps.what: Clarify the buyer's question and intended use.
Check account prices, stock and approved credit terms in the {ERP}.
Find product uses, limitations and warranty guidance in approved documents.

loop.input: Clarified question and retrieved passages from current approved documents.
loop.output: Relevant guidance with document version, passage citations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Verify citations and document versions; reject unsupported statements and conflicting guidance.
loop.stop: At most two retrieval rounds and one extraction; missing or conflicting evidence goes to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Product uses and limitations are often buried in prose. Structured facts use direct lookup.

steps.what: Explain the answer and resolve questions about the buyer's situation.
Send written confirmation of the answer and supporting information.
Record the question, answer and follow-up in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: An answer desk in the {CRM} retrieves account-specific commercial facts from the {ERP} and cited guidance from {DOCS}. Configured templates assemble confirmations for representative approval in {EMAIL}, then update the {CRM}; a bounded extraction loop handles prose manuals. A small {BI} view groups recorded questions to reveal recurring information gaps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account prices and stock sat apart from product documents. Keeping access permissions, document versions and answers aligned required integration and upkeep.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces and templates handle factual lookup. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting them, while bounded extraction helps with prose manuals.
tasks.still_hard: Fresh availability, account-specific terms, conflicting manuals and unusual product uses still need careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a simple question hides a suitability concern, commercial objection or damaged relationship.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on which recurring product-information gaps to fix.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time searching and more time resolving uncertain uses and commercial exceptions. They can prioritise information improvements; pricing and credit authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check availability and explain order status.
reach.learn: Distinguish physical stock, available-to-promise stock and unconfirmed delivery estimates.

evidence.claim: Record-based answers can use deterministic lookup; prose manuals may need bounded extraction.
Elfsquad connects product configuration with commercial systems, supporting adjacent product-information lookup.
The documented chatbot fare dispute illustrates exposure from incorrect customer-facing answers.
Customer-facing AI interaction requires disclosure under EU AI Act Article 50.

assumptions: This is a typical mixed channel workflow; time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The bounded model output remains internal. Written confirmations use approved templates and a human release gate.
Structured question fields replace duplicate logging without assuming call recording.
GDPR applies to buyer and employee records. EU AI Act duties depend on deployment; national rules determine consultation requirements.
Effort ranges assume usable interfaces and include access, permissions, rollout and consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Which account prices, credit terms and stock fields are authoritative and accessible?
Which manuals have owners, versions and approved translations?
Can the existing {CRM} configure templates, interaction capture and account-level permissions?
Would the proposed reporting introduce employee monitoring requiring national consultation?
research_questions: How often do questions require interpretation beyond approved documents?
What data freshness is needed before an availability answer becomes misleading?
Which question categories can use fixed templates without a model?
new_work: Review confirmations before sending.
Resolve conflicting documents and missing account facts.
Maintain document ownership, lookup mappings and templates.
Sample cited guidance and review recurring unanswered questions.
tasks.statement: Answer customers' questions about products, prices, availability, product uses, and credit terms.

tasks.short: Recommend suitable products based on the buyer's needs, constraints and preferences.

steps.what: Discuss intended use, budget, delivery needs and preferences with the buyer.
Review the buyer's previous purchases and recorded preferences in the {CRM}.
Compare catalogue specifications and identify products meeting the stated constraints.
Choose a recommendation and identify trade-offs or unanswered suitability questions.
Explain the recommendation, demonstrate relevant features and discuss alternatives.
Record the recommendation, buyer feedback and next action in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A structured needs form in the {CRM} feeds a deterministic comparison tool using approved catalogue attributes from {DOCS} and current price and availability from the {ERP}. It filters hard constraints, shows trade-offs and reruns when requirements change; the representative chooses and explains the recommendation. Selected products and structured feedback populate a reviewable {CRM} record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Catalogue attributes were inconsistent, and buyer preferences lived in conversations. Building and maintaining a useful comparison tool required substantial manual mapping.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small comparison tool cheaper to build. Explicit product constraints and structured needs capture provide the underlying logic.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete specifications, unstated preferences, unfamiliar uses and competing priorities resist simple scoring.
tasks.human_edge: Discover what the buyer values, challenge an unsuitable request and explain a trade-off credibly.

ambition.what: Reassess product fit during the discussion whenever budget or delivery requirements change.

tasks.altitude: The representative compares alternatives during the buyer discussion instead of researching them afterwards. They retain recommendation responsibility; no new commercial approval rights are assumed.

reach.task: Validate compatibility and unusual product applications.
reach.learn: Separate hard exclusions from preferences and recognise when specialist validation is necessary.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad supports rule-based product configuration connected to commercial systems.
Explicit constraints can narrow a shortlist without automating the buyer's preferences or the representative's judgement.
The proposed time reductions and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: Most recommendations concern established catalogue goods with identifiable constraints.
Automated filtering covers explicit requirements only; missing critical attributes trigger specialist review.
Existing configuration features are checked before building a comparison tool.
Structured notes are captured during the discussion; automatic recording or transcription is not assumed.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act requirements apply. National rules determine consultation where employee data use changes.
Effort includes initial catalogue mapping, access, user trials and applicable consultation.
unknowns: Are product specifications available as maintained structured attributes?
Does existing software already provide adequate configuration or comparison?
Which applications require specialist validation?
Are purchase history and account preferences accessible in the {CRM}?
research_questions: Which constraints eliminate unsuitable products reliably?
How often do experienced representatives reject a technically valid shortlist?
Which missing attributes cause the most manual research?
new_work: Maintain catalogue attributes and hard exclusions.
Investigate empty or unexpectedly broad shortlists.
Review generated recommendation records.
Check whether changing specifications invalidate existing comparison rules.
tasks.statement: Recommend products to customers, based on customers' needs and interests.

tasks.short: Contact customers, demonstrate products, explain features and seek orders.

steps.what: Review account history, open opportunities and recent orders in the {CRM}.
Select product sheets and demonstration materials from the {DOCS}.
Arrange a call or visit through {EMAIL} and the {CALENDAR}.
Demonstrate products, discuss needs, answer questions and seek an order during the visit.
Record requirements, objections and follow-up actions in the {CRM}.

loop.input: Representative's written meeting notes and the existing opportunity record.
loop.output: Proposed requirement fields, objections and follow-up actions, each linked to a note passage.
loop.check: Validate field types and account identity; the representative checks meaning and commitments before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one validation retry; unresolved fields remain blank for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes express requirements and commitments in varying language; field mapping alone loses meaning.

steps.what: Forward the order request and supporting details to the order clerk through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure an account brief in the {CRM}, assemble approved materials from the {DOCS}, and prepare appointment invitations through the {CALENDAR}. A bounded extraction loop turns written meeting notes into reviewed {CRM} updates; a configured workflow routes completed order requests to the order clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account context, product documents and order handoffs sit in separate places. Useful meeting details arrive as free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing views and scheduling features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes document assembly and small integrations cheaper; bounded extraction reduces repeated typing.
tasks.still_hard: Live demonstrations, reading buying signals and resolving unfamiliar product questions require experience. Product documents must stay current.
tasks.human_edge: The representative earns trust, notices hesitation and adapts the demonstration to the buyer's situation.

ambition.what: Application-specific demonstration packs for smaller repeat customers.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less preparation and transcription, leaving room for more tailored demonstrations. Commercial approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Validate whether an order request is ready for entry.
reach.learn: Required item identifiers, quantities, delivery details and escalation rules.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad links product configuration to CRM and ERP, supporting rule-based preparation of product selections and quotes.
Written-note extraction can be bounded by field validation, source passages and human approval; live selling remains human.
In the Netherlands, seller activity monitoring can require works council consent; requirements elsewhere depend on national rules.

assumptions: The setting is a mid-size European wholesaler or manufacturer with account records in the {CRM} and approved product materials in the {DOCS}.
Visits are the representative case; remote demonstrations use similar preparation and follow-up.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings. The conversation remains the largest part.
Order routing creates an internal handoff; order acceptance follows the existing order process.
The access range includes GDPR review and applicable employee consultation under national rules. EU AI Act requirements apply where relevant.
unknowns: Whether account records contain current order history.
Whether product sheets have reliable item identifiers and approval status.
Whether contact permissions and scheduling rules are recorded.
Whether the proposed record processing requires employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can existing {CRM} views and appointment features cover the account brief and scheduling?
How accurately can written notes populate required fields without inventing commitments?
new_work: Review proposed meeting records and appointment invitations.
Maintain product-to-document mappings and approved templates.
Resolve incomplete order handoffs and monitor integration failures.
Sample extracted fields for omissions and incorrect commitments.
tasks.statement: Contact regular and prospective customers to demonstrate products, explain product features, and solicit orders.

tasks.short: Prepare and explain quotes covering prices, terms, warranties and estimated delivery dates.

steps.what: Clarify quantities, product choices, delivery requirements and requested terms with the buyer.
Check account pricing, stock, lead times and existing credit terms in the {ERP}.
Calculate line prices, discounts, freight and quote totals in a spreadsheet.
Select approved warranty and contract wording for the proposed sale.
Review and approve requested discounts outside the representative's authority.
Decide whether to approve requested credit terms outside existing account limits.
Assemble the quote document with approved prices, terms and delivery estimates.
Explain the proposed offer and negotiate requested changes with the buyer.
Check the final quote and send it to the buyer.

tasks.design: Configure quoting in the {CRM} or {ERP} with approved product rules, calculations and templates from {DOCS}; use a deterministic connector where existing links are insufficient. The {WORKFLOW} routes discount and credit exceptions to their authorised approvers, invalidates approvals after material changes and requires representative approval before {EMAIL} release. Price-version changes in the {ERP} flag affected open quotes in the {CRM} for repricing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prices, terms and approvals were maintained separately. Bespoke quoting logic and reliable links were costly to implement and keep aligned.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration handles much of the quoting logic. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of connectors, validation and document assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Negotiated exceptions, uncertain supply dates, inconsistent price data and non-standard contract language remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Judge the commercial trade-off, negotiate credibly and avoid promises the business cannot fulfil.

ambition.what: Reprice affected open quotes when supplier price changes reach the {ERP}.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time calculating and assembling documents, and more time negotiating viable offers. Existing discount and credit limits remain in force; no new approval rights are assumed.

reach.task: Review discount exceptions and commercial exposure.
reach.learn: Explain margin, freight and payment-term effects when proposing a concession.

reach.task: Convert an accepted quote into an accurate order.
reach.learn: Maintain item identifiers, quote versions and approval references through the handoff.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad provides rule-based configuration and quoting linked to commercial systems.
The ZARGES vendor case reports quoting time falling from about 15 minutes to 90 seconds.
Structured quoting calculations, clause selection and approval routing generally do not need a model.

assumptions: The typical baseline uses the {ERP} for facts, with a spreadsheet bridging calculations and document preparation.
Approval steps are conditional; their time shares represent effort across the quote portfolio.
Negotiated changes repeat affected calculation and approval steps before release.
Only approved clause variants are selected automatically; non-standard terms require separate authorised review.
Unconfirmed delivery dates remain estimates. Existing account credit terms are retrieved without introducing automated credit scoring.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act requirements apply. National rules govern consultation where relevant.
Effort assumes configurable quoting is available and includes access, approval testing and rollout.
unknowns: What quoting configuration and integration features are already licensed?
Which discounts and terms can the representative approve?
Who approves non-standard contract wording?
Can the {ERP} distinguish confirmed delivery promises from estimates?
Are supplier price changes versioned against open quotes?
research_questions: Which quote variants account for most manual assembly?
How often do changes invalidate earlier approvals?
Which calculation discrepancies most often cause order-entry rework?
new_work: Maintain pricing rules, templates and approval thresholds.
Resolve missing prices and uncertain delivery dates.
Review exceptions and final quote release.
Review repricing alerts and decide whether to revise open offers.
Check that negotiated changes invalidate affected approvals.
tasks.statement: Estimate or quote prices, credit or contract terms, warranties, and delivery dates.

tasks.short: Support buyers after a sale, resolve problems and coordinate agreed remedies.

steps.what: Listen to the buyer's problem and clarify its impact and desired outcome.
Review the account history and link the issue to the relevant order.
Check product guidance, warranty coverage and relevant support procedures.

loop.input: Case brief and current approved product, warranty and support documents.
loop.output: Cited procedures, possible exclusions and questions needing human assessment.
loop.check: Verify product and document versions, exact source passages and applicability dates; do not infer entitlement.
loop.stop: At most two retrieval rounds and one extraction; unresolved coverage or conflicting procedures go to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative fault descriptions and procedural documents require language matching; fixed identifiers use direct lookup.

steps.what: Send the issue and evidence to operations for investigation.
Investigate the issue and confirm feasible remedies and timing.
Discuss the options and agree a remedy or support plan with the buyer.
Record agreed actions, owners and due dates in the {CRM}.
Send the agreed follow-up and check whether the issue is resolved.

tasks.design: A linked case view in the {CRM} reads orders from the {ERP}, operational status from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and cited support guidance from {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes internal requests, tracks owners and deadlines, and prepares approved-template follow-ups for representative release through {EMAIL}. Confirmed delivery events also create first-use check-in tasks in the {CRM}, while investigation and remedy conversations remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case context was scattered across messages, account records and operational records. Follow-up depended on individual memory and manual chasing.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured cases, event triggers and templates already cover much of the coordination. Cheaper integrations and bounded document extraction reduce preparation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Physical faults, disputed responsibility, supplier dependencies and rebuilding trust still require people.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the buyer's frustration, take credible responsibility and negotiate a remedy that both sides can accept.

ambition.what: Scheduled first-use support for first-time business buyers.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time reconstructing cases and chasing updates, with more time for difficult recovery conversations and planned support. Remedy and compensation authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Plan post-sale check-ins and confirm that the buyer receives the intended benefit.
reach.learn: Use milestones and buyer outcomes to structure useful follow-up conversations.

reach.task: Assess escalated complaints and proposed commercial remedies.
reach.learn: Present customer impact, feasible options and commercial consequences clearly.

evidence.claim: Case linking, internal routing, deadlines and template follow-ups can use deterministic workflows.
Bounded extraction can prepare cited guidance while leaving entitlement and remedy decisions to people.
The digest contains no documented case measuring this complete post-sale support workflow.

assumptions: The baseline uses the {CRM} and internal messages for coordination; an existing {HELPDESK} should be configured instead if it already owns support cases.
The operations step covers investigation and feasible options, not every downstream repair, replacement or refund activity.
Structured remedy fields are confirmed by the representative; no automatic call recording is assumed.
Human conversations act within existing authority. Out-of-authority compensation requires the existing approval process before commitment.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act requirements apply. National rules determine employee consultation and monitoring restrictions.
Effort includes case permissions, access, consultation where applicable, realistic exception trials and rollout.
unknowns: Does the {CRM} or {HELPDESK} own the authoritative support case?
Can customer accounts, orders and operational incidents be linked reliably?
Who may authorise replacements, refunds and compensation?
Are delivery events and remedy completion updates reliable enough to trigger follow-up?
What access and national consultation requirements apply to shared case reporting?
research_questions: Which delays arise from missing context rather than physical investigation?
Which support procedures can be retrieved reliably by product and issue type?
When do first-time buyers benefit most from a first-use check-in?
new_work: Review case updates and customer follow-ups.
Resolve unmatched orders and contradictory support guidance.
Maintain routing, escalation paths and document versions.
Check overdue actions and delivery-trigger failures.
Conduct the new first-use check-ins and record their outcomes.
tasks.statement: Consult with clients after sales or contract signings to resolve problems and to provide ongoing support.

tasks.short: Translate customer requirements into suitable drawings, estimates, and bids.

steps.what: Read the customer request and extract quantities, dimensions, dates, and requested options.

loop.output: Structured requirements with source references and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate units and required fields; show source passages for quantities, dimensions, and deadlines.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per request; ambiguous or missing requirements go to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests arrive as varied prose and documents. Structured forms can replace this loop where customers use them.

steps.what: Clarify intended use, constraints, and priorities with the customer.
Select suitable products and identify departures from standard configurations.
Adapt a standard drawing in the {OTHER} drawing tool to the selected products.
Calculate quantities, prices, freight, lead times, and margin in the estimate workbook.
Assemble the bid with drawings, estimated prices, scope, assumptions, and exclusions.
Review bid completeness and approve commercial exceptions.
Send the approved bid and record its version and follow-up date.

tasks.design: Configure product rules and pricing in {ERP} where supported, and use deterministic generators for estimates, bid templates in {DOCS}, and standard drawings through {OTHER}. A bounded extraction loop converts requests from {EMAIL} into a requirements brief; the representative confirms fit, and {WORKFLOW} releases the exact approved bid and records follow-up in {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrive in mixed formats, while product rules, drawings, prices, and bid documents are maintained separately. Bespoke combinations resist simple templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configurators demonstrate controlled quoting. Faster coding makes template generation and record connections more affordable, with bounded extraction for unstructured requests.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete specifications, unusual combinations, drawing-library maintenance, and reliable delivery commitments. Novel drawings still need a competent person.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the customer's intended use and notice where a plausible configuration fails in practice.

ambition.what: Side-by-side bids for a standard option and a lower-cost alternative

tasks.altitude: The representative spends more time clarifying needs and comparing alternatives, with less copying between drawings and estimates. They can explore more options within existing pricing limits; formal approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Check fit and constraints when a requested layout exceeds standard drawing rules.
reach.learn: Dimensional tolerances, installation constraints, and the boundary between illustrative and technical drawings.

reach.task: Convert accepted bid lines into an accurate order.
reach.learn: Item identifiers, option codes, units, delivery commitments, and version matching.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad offers configuration and quoting linked to ERP and CRM records.
The ZARGES vendor case reports quote preparation falling from about 15 minutes to 90 seconds.
Parametric templates can generate standard drawings; the digest does not establish coverage for bespoke drawings.
Bounded extraction can support varied customer requests when source references and field checks accompany review.

assumptions: Drawings are sales layouts or product illustrations, not engineering certification.
A useful share of bids follows standard product and drawing families.
The scenario includes a workbook joining prices, freight, and margin; some firms already calculate these in {ERP}.
Manager review is averaged across cases and may be limited to exceptions.
Bid release uses the approval recorded in the preceding review step.
The judgement-heavy prior applies to fit and clarification; standard calculations and document assembly have greater rule coverage.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates; creating a missing product-rule library would add substantial work.
unknowns: Share of standard versus bespoke drawings and bids.
Whether product combinations, pricing, freight, and lead-time rules are maintained.
Drawing tool interfaces and template licensing.
Who approves product suitability and commercial exceptions.
Whether the representative can access current stock and margin data.
research_questions: Which product families support deterministic drawing generation?
Can existing {ERP} configuration replace the estimate workbook?
What extraction accuracy is achievable on representative historical requests?
Which fields need explicit customer confirmation before a bid is issued?
What national consultation is required if bid records change employee monitoring?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and resolve ambiguous units or dimensions.
Maintain configuration rules, drawing templates, prices, and freight rates.
Route bespoke drawings and unusual product combinations to specialists.
Check stale availability and delivery assumptions.
Resolve generation failures and retain approved bid versions.
tasks.statement: Prepare drawings, estimates, and bids that meet specific customer needs.

tasks.short: Choose and provide product samples and relevant catalogs to customers.

steps.what: Discuss the customer's intended use and sample needs.
Choose samples and catalog sections using product information in the {DOCS}.
Check sample availability and permitted quantities in the {ERP}.
Send the selected catalog to the customer through the {EMAIL}.
Request selected samples from the warehouse through the {EMAIL}.
Pick, pack and dispatch the requested physical samples.
Present samples and explain differences during the customer visit.
Record sample delivery, customer feedback and follow-up in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Use a sample-request form in the {CRM} to check the {ERP}, send selected catalogs from the {DOCS}, and create warehouse requests in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Delivery events update sample history automatically, while people select products, handle physical samples and discuss customer reactions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical samples and customer conversations dominated the task. Small requests were passed through a mailbox without a shared delivery record.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, stock lookups and notifications can connect the administrative steps. A model adds little to this flow.
tasks.still_hard: Texture, finish, fit and practical suitability require physical evaluation. Sample stock may not be recorded as ordinary saleable stock.
tasks.human_edge: The representative notices hesitation and helps customers compare physical qualities that a catalog cannot convey.

ambition.what: A remote sample-request service for small repeat buyers

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time chasing parcels and attaching catalogs. They gain visibility into sample follow-up, but no additional pricing or fulfilment approval rights.

reach.task: Run a structured comparison of competing sample options.
reach.learn: Demonstration techniques and questions that reveal practical suitability.

reach.task: Coordinate sample dispatch and resolve address or stock exceptions.
reach.learn: Warehouse request fields and delivery-status handling.

evidence.claim: Forms, stock checks and dispatch notifications can automate sample administration without replacing physical demonstrations.

assumptions: Catalogs are approved public materials and are sent in response to customer requests.
Physical handling and customer discussion dominate, consistent with the human-work prior.
Shares include warehouse labour associated with fulfilling sample requests.
GDPR applies to contact details and delivery addresses. National rules govern promotional communications; EU AI Act duties apply if AI is later added.
unknowns: Are sample items and quantities recorded in the {ERP} or {OPS_SYSTEM}?
Which sample requests require approval because of value or restricted products?
Can customers request samples remotely today?
Who maintains current catalogs and language variants?
research_questions: Can requested catalogs and sample dispatch use existing configuration?
Which sample requests most often fail because of stock or address problems?
Would small repeat buyers use a remote request form?
new_work: Maintain catalog versions and sample-request limits.
Handle missing stock, incorrect addresses and failed delivery events.
Capture customer feedback and choose the next follow-up action.
Keep sample availability records accurate.
tasks.statement: Provide customers with product samples and catalogs.

tasks.short: Find prospective customers through directories, referrals, professional networks and trade events.

steps.what: Review target segments and existing account coverage in the {CRM}.
Search business directories in {OTHER} for companies matching the target segment.
Read customer referrals in {EMAIL} and identify suggested companies and contacts.

loop.input: Selected referral messages with sender and message date.
loop.output: Suggested company, contact, referral context and supporting message passages.
loop.check: Check contact formats and company matches; a representative confirms ambiguous identities and referral meaning.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per message; ambiguous referrals enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Referrals use varied language and often imply the relationship without structured fields.

steps.what: Meet contacts at trade events and professional gatherings to discover buying needs.
Assess commercial fit and select prospects for follow-up in the {CRM}.
Check duplicates and create lead records and follow-up tasks in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure segment and territory views in the {CRM}, then import permitted structured directory data from {OTHER} with deterministic matching and provenance. A bounded loop extracts referrals from selected {EMAIL} messages; the representative qualifies prospects, while configured duplicate checks and task creation complete the records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prospect information arrives through unrelated directories, referrals and events. Manual identity matching and record entry make small prospects expensive to research.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured imports and existing duplicate checks handle routine records. AI-assisted coding lowers integration effort, while a small extraction loop handles referral language.
tasks.still_hard: Buying intent and referral strength are often known only through conversation. Directory access, permitted reuse and company identity quality vary.
tasks.human_edge: The representative recognises promising relationships and earns introductions that a directory cannot supply.

ambition.what: Small regional resellers previously below the prospect-research threshold.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time collecting and entering company details and more time developing introductions. Prospect selection remains within existing territory and qualification rights.

reach.task: Assess coverage gaps across territories and customer segments.
reach.learn: Segment definitions, territory conflicts and the difference between list size and commercial potential.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales documents lead research and qualification agents. This establishes capability, not a need for autonomous agents here.
Structured directory imports, duplicate checks and bounded referral extraction can support prospect discovery without automating networking.
GDPR applies to identifiable business contacts; outreach permissions also depend on channel and national rules.

assumptions: A permitted structured directory export or interface is available; its subscription cost is separate from build time.
The {CRM} supports lead staging, duplicate checks and follow-up tasks.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates. Networking remains the dominant activity, consistent with the relationship-heavy priors.
Qualification time falls because source evidence and existing-account matches arrive together.
The access range includes data-use review, GDPR requirements and applicable employee consultation under national rules; EU AI Act requirements apply where relevant.
unknowns: Which directory data may legally and contractually be reused.
How territory ownership and duplicate account disputes are resolved.
Whether referral messages contain usable contact details.
Which national outreach and employee consultation rules apply.
research_questions: What proportion of directory candidates match existing accounts or inactive leads?
Which qualification criteria are objective enough to display as filters?
Can ambiguous company matches be isolated without delaying clean imports?
new_work: Review ambiguous company matches and extracted referrals.
Maintain target filters, source permissions and retention rules.
Correct stale contacts and process objections or deletion requests.
Monitor import failures and directory schema changes.
tasks.statement: Identify prospective customers by using business directories, following leads from existing clients, participating in organizations and clubs, and attending trade shows and conferences.

tasks.short: Coordinate product delivery and installation with customers, logistics staff and installation providers.

steps.what: Review the confirmed order, delivery deadline and installation scope.
Clarify site access, readiness and acceptable delivery windows with the customer.
Request carrier and installer availability against customer requirements.
Agree a feasible sequence and resolve timing conflicts with the parties.
Check the plan, book delivery and installation, and issue instructions.
Check delivery progress and flag missed milestones.
Resolve delivery problems and obtain customer confirmation of completion.
Record completion and route unresolved installation issues.

tasks.design: A case in the {WORKFLOW} combines order requirements from the {ERP}, structured readiness forms and provider availability. Deterministic checks propose feasible windows, issue approved bookings and compare status from the {OPS_SYSTEM} against the delivery plan. The representative handles readiness conversations and disputed changes; structured completion confirmation updates the {ERP} and routes open issues.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer readiness, carrier capacity and installer schedules sit with different parties. Email and calls carry details that never reach a shared schedule.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, calendar links and status integrations can collect the minimum scheduling data. AI-assisted coding makes the small connectors and constraint checks cheaper to build; no model is required for the proposed pilot.
tasks.still_hard: Site conditions change and provider status can be late. People must negotiate disruption, extra charges and customer acceptance; installation providers retain technical and safety responsibilities.
tasks.human_edge: The representative reads customer readiness, balances competing commitments and restores trust when delivery or installation goes wrong.

ambition.what: Pre-delivery readiness review for customers receiving their first installed product.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer availability chases and status checks, leaving more time for readiness reviews and difficult rescheduling. Booking and compensation authority stays within existing limits.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of non-retail sales workers
reach.task: Resolve delivery escalations across several customer accounts.
reach.learn: Capacity constraints, escalation thresholds and the commercial cost of competing delivery promises.

evidence.claim: Structured availability, scheduling constraints, milestone comparisons and reminders are deterministic workflow functions.
Site readiness discussions and disputed delivery changes need contextual human coordination, while preparation and completion records can be automated.
The digest provides no documented end-to-end case for delivery and installation coordination in this occupation.

assumptions: The baseline is a mid-size European seller coordinating delivery and straightforward installation through internal logistics or external providers.
The representative coordinates installation rather than performing or certifying technical work.
Step shares represent active staff time, not waiting time, and require customer validation.
Human coordination remains the largest activity, consistent with the supplied prior; email chasing is a separate removable component.
Providers can use structured availability and completion forms. Non-response enters the human exception queue.
Booking checks include order version, capacity, installation sequence and duplicate booking prevention.
Build ranges cover a limited provider pilot in working days. Access or consultation delays may exceed the estimate.
GDPR applies to contact and site data. Access work includes employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which products require installation and who accepts installation completion.
Whether provider availability and delivery status are accessible through supported interfaces.
Actual scheduling effort, disruption frequency and provider response times.
Who can approve extra charges, changed dates and compensation.
Whether employee consultation agreements cover the proposed status logging.
research_questions: Can current workflow and calendar configuration cover structured availability collection without custom code?
Which readiness checks predict failed visits for the selected product category?
Which national rules and internal agreements apply if delivery tracking also observes employee activity?
new_work: Review proposed bookings before external commitments.
Chase providers who do not return structured availability or completion records.
Resolve readiness conflicts, stale status and disputed completion.
Maintain scheduling constraints, provider contacts and escalation thresholds.
Check integration failures, access permissions and retention settings.
tasks.statement: Arrange and direct delivery and installation of products and equipment.

tasks.short: Track market changes, product innovations and competitor offerings to inform sales decisions.

steps.what: Read trade publications and competitor pages using a browser and the {DOCS}.
Ask customers and distributors about demand, alternatives and observed prices.
Update competitor comparisons and source notes in the {SPREADSHEET}.

loop.input: Approved source documents and manually captured market observations.

steps.what: Compare observations with internal sales trends in the {ERP} and {BI}.

tasks.short: Maintain sales records, prepare budgets and reports, and submit expense claims.

tasks.still_hard: Returns, credits, revenue timing and account ownership can distort totals. Forecast assumptions and expense legitimacy remain human judgements.
tasks.human_edge: The representative explains why an account will grow or shrink and supplies honest business context that transaction records cannot establish.
